th_east_edge.name: Thornwold Edge
th_east_edge.desc: The Vale's young ash gives way to old growth, black-barked and older than any road cut through it. A blazoned board reads FREE FOR HIRE, TOLL FOR OTHERS. Woodsmoke shows west toward Camp Gallows; open sky and the Vale wait east.

th_north_track.name: The North Track
th_north_track.desc: The old growth thins northward into scrub and gray spoil-dust, blown down off the Iron Downs on every wind. Deep cart-ruts run through here, cut by ore-wagons that never once paid Camp Gallows its toll. South, the wood closes back over the camp.

th_south_track.name: The South Track
th_south_track.desc: The old growth breaks into scrub pine and, past it, a taste of salt on the wind that has no business this far from any coast. Gull-cries carry faint from the south. North, woodsmoke marks the camp.
th_south_track.brief: A taste of salt, gulls crying.

th_settlement.name: Camp Gallows — Palisade Gate
th_settlement.desc: A ring of sharpened stakes and old rope, three roads meeting at its one gate. A dead oak stands just inside, hung with rope nobody has cut down — the camp took its name from it, though nobody living remembers why. A sentry eyes your purse more than your face.
th_settlement.brief: The palisade. The old hanging oak.

variants.desc: The dead oak stands black as ever inside the palisade, but the wind now carries a second smoke from west in the wood, one that does not smell of cooking fires.
variants.brief: The palisade. A second smoke, west.
The palisade. The old oak, quiet now.
The palisade. The camp keeps an odd, solemn quiet.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: West along the middle row, four stands: the gallows road. North-west past the black thorn: the Understory, Ness's hut. South-west the Denhollow; south the Long Watch; north the Cutter's Barrow; Rook north-west.

th_muster.name: The Muster Ground
th_muster.desc: Packed dirt, scarred by drillwork. A dozen off-duty mercenaries dice or mend gear in loose knots, none of them looking twice at a stranger who isn't buying. Captain Vane's tent stands north; the quartermaster's wagon east; the cook-fire west.
th_muster.brief: Packed dirt, dice and mended gear.

variants.desc: Packed dirt, scarred by drillwork. The dicing has stopped; nobody here will say why out loud. Captain Vane's tent stands north; the quartermaster's wagon east; the cook-fire west.
variants.brief: Packed dirt. The dicing has stopped.
Packed dirt. Easier laughter than before.
Packed dirt. One less voice than there was.

th_captains_tent.name: Captain Vane's Tent
th_captains_tent.desc: Patched canvas over a camp table cluttered with tally-sticks and a Reach map gone soft at the folds. Captain Sorrel Vane stands over it rather than sits, the way a soldier stands who has learned chairs are for staying too long.
th_captains_tent.brief: A cluttered table, and Captain Vane.

th_quartermaster.name: The Quartermaster's Wagon
th_quartermaster.desc: A covered wagon doubles as counter and strongroom both, ledgers stacked against the damp. Quartermaster Bray keeps one hand on the tally at all times, as if the numbers might otherwise wander off on their own.

actions.label: buy a jug of pitch-oil (8 gold)
fx: Bray weighs the jug once and hands it over without a single question about what it's for.

actions.label: clear Cal's debt at the wagon (10 gold)
fx: Bray marks the ledger square and says nothing more about it. That's debt enough to send a man home with a clean name, if he'll take it.

actions.label: search the dead-letter box (wits)
fx: Under a decade of unsent requisitions, one letter never left camp: a pardon, signed at Marrowgate, addressed to a captain forty years dead. Nobody thought to burn it. Nobody thought to send it either.
Paper on paper, none of it wants to be found. It can be tried again.

th_stockade.name: The Stockade
th_stockade.desc: A cage of green-cut poles, roofed against the rain and not much else. A man sits inside with his knees drawn up, watching you with more curiosity than a prisoner usually spares a stranger.
th_stockade.brief: A pole cage. A watchful prisoner.

th_cookfire.name: The Cook-Fire
th_cookfire.desc: A great iron pot hangs over coals that never quite go out. The cook ladles without looking up, and the smell alone is worth the walk from the muster ground.
th_cookfire.brief: An iron pot, coals banked low.

actions.label: eat by the cook-fire
fx: A bowl of something thick and unnamed, and a fire that asks nothing of you. You eat until you're steadier.

th_scout_line.name: The Scout Line
th_scout_line.desc: A row of stakes hung with straw targets, arrows bristling from most of them. A young man in faded Company colors nocks another shaft, form good and aim better — he has the look of someone who took up a bow to stop thinking about something else.

th_understory_root.name: The Black Thorn Gap
th_understory_root.desc: A gap in the thornbrake, easy to miss and easier to lose again once found. Beyond it the ground drops into root and shadow, and something like a doorway shows in the dark where no doorway ought to be.

down.lockedMsg: The dark past the doorway gives you nothing to hold onto, and you lose the way again.
down.hint: find the way through (grace or wits)

actions.label: press through the dark, blind (grace)
fx: Your hand finds a root worn smooth as a rail, and the dark opens ahead of it rather than around it. There's a way through here, if you keep the feel of it.
The dark gives nothing back. You end up exactly where you started, thorn-scratched for the trouble.

actions.label: read the wear on the roots (wits)
fx: One root is worn paler than the rest, a path polished by feet that came this way on purpose, over years. You follow the polish, not the dark.
Every root looks the same as every other. It can be tried again.

th_understory_hall.name: The Understory
th_understory_hall.desc: Root and hollow trunk, grown or coaxed into something like a room. Keeper Rowan sits cross-legged over a bundle of bark-strips scored with old marks, and looks up at you the way a woodsman looks up at weather.
th_understory_hall.brief: Root and hollow trunk. Keeper Rowan.

th_hollow_approach.name: The Silent Reach
th_hollow_approach.desc: The wood goes quiet by degrees until it is entirely quiet — no birds, no wind in the leaves, though the leaves still move. Bootprints and older things print the wet ground, none of them recent, all of them headed the same way.
onEnterOnce: So this is Thornwold's grief. Even the wood knows to keep its distance.

th_hollow_gate.name: The Waiting Bough
th_hollow_gate.desc: A bough arches low over the path, and one of the hanged still keeps his post beneath it — forty years gray, the rope long rotted to nothing but the shape of a noose still holding his neck at its old angle. He turns to face you before you're within ten strides.
th_hollow_gate.brief: The hanged sergeant bars the bough.

west.lockedMsg: The gray sergeant will not step aside for anyone who hasn't answered him.
west.hint: fight him, slip past (grace), or answer him plain (will)

variants.desc: The bough stands empty now, the old rope swaying with nothing in it. Whatever kept its post here has finally stood down.

actions.label: slip past him along the bough (grace)
fx: You keep to the far side of the bough and go quiet where he's slow. He turns to find nothing, and doesn't turn again.
The bough is narrower than it looked. You're back on the path, and he hasn't moved.

actions.label: answer the sergeant plainly (will)
fx: You say it plain: the charge was never proven, and he knows it better than you do. Something in the set of his shoulders finally loosens. He steps from the path and does not block it again.
He hears you out and does not move. Whatever he's waiting to hear, that wasn't it.

th_hollow_glade.name: The Gallows Glade
th_hollow_glade.desc: The hanging tree stands at the glade's heart, and the Company hangs from it still — a dozen shapes gone gray and thin, turning though there is no wind to turn them. The ground beneath has not grown so much as a blade of grass in forty years.
onEnterOnce: However this ends — rite, oath, or fire — it ends here, and it ends once.

variants.name: The Waking Glade
variants.desc: The hanging tree still stands, but it holds only itself now. New grass has begun to push up pale through last year's char, unhurried about it.

variants.name: The Sworn Glade
variants.desc: The tree stands bare of its dead, but the ground beneath it is trampled fresh — the living Company musters here now, once a year, to say the old names aloud.

variants.name: The Burned Glade
variants.desc: The hanging tree is a black stub, and the ground around it is ash going to char going to nothing at all. Whatever grieved here has stopped, one way or another.
variants.brief: A black stub. Ash and char.

actions.label: read the true pardon over them
fx: You read the pardon whole, forty years late, every name on it spoken aloud. The turning stops. One by one they settle, and the tree is only a tree.

actions.label: speak the Keeper's verse over them
fx: You speak the verse Keeper Rowan taught you, plain and unhurried. Whatever it says, it says what they needed to hear — the turning slows, and stops, and does not start again.

actions.label: speak the rest-oath from memory (will)
fx: You give them what words you have, half-remembered and meant anyway. It's enough. The turning stops, and the glade goes as still as any ordinary wood.
The words won't come whole. Whatever's needed here, half a rest-oath isn't it. It can be tried again.

actions.label: swear the Company's oath (will)
fx: The living Company files in behind you and swears the old oath in the dead men's own names, Captain Vane leading it. The hanging tree empties itself, name by name, into the mouths of the living.
The oath comes out ragged, more mutter than vow. Nothing in the glade moves. It can be tried again.

actions.label: burn it — a failed try costs 1hp (might)
fx: The oil catches fast and the tree with it, forty years of grief burning off in one bad hour. The turning stops because there is nothing left to turn. The Ironbound would call this clean.
The oil won't take in the damp, and something in the smoke catches your throat wrong. It can be tried again.

th_hollow_grave.name: The Fallen Muster
th_hollow_grave.desc: Personal effects gone to mold at the tree's roots — a boot, a dice-cup, a tin box nobody thought to seal properly. Whatever fell with the Company forty years ago is still falling apart down here, slower than it should.

actions.label: search the tin box
fx: Five old coins and a muster-roll page gone soft, one name ringed twice in fading ink — a rival officer's, not one of the hanged. Whoever wrote that ring knew more than they ever said.

th_pitch_oil.name: a jug of pitch-oil
th_pitch_oil.hint: the Ironbound's own recipe — carries fire further than it has any right to

th_pardon.name: the true pardon, unsent
th_pardon.hint: signed at Marrowgate, forty years late — read it where the Company can hear it

variants.hint: read over the Hanged Company, forty years late

th_free_blade.name: a Free Company blade
th_free_blade.hint: well-balanced, better kept than most Company steel

th_bitter_bark.name: bitter forest bark
th_bitter_bark.hint: chew it to ease a wound

fx: Bitter as the name promises, but the ache dulls fast.

th_boar_tusk.name: a gray boar's tusk
th_boar_tusk.hint: Sergeant Coe might want to see it

th_vane.name: Captain Sorrel Vane
th_vane.desc: Weathered past the age most soldiers retire, one hand always near her belt, never on it.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Captain of what's left of the Free Company. We hire out to anyone with coin and no army of their own. You're standing in the middle of it.

topics.label: the hanging tree
topics.say: Forty years back the Company that camped here got hanged for a mutiny nobody I've spoken to still believes. We took the ground and the name anyway. Somebody had to hold it.

topics.label: propose the Company swear an oath
topics.say: ...You're not wrong that we owe them something. I'll bring the Company to the glade myself, when you're ready to lead the words. Don't waste it.

topics.label: the road under Coldpass
topics.say: There's a smugglers' stair down in the Saltkerns that skips Coldpass' gate entirely. I'll sell you the road — coin, or a favor worth the same to me.

topics.label: pay for the smugglers' road (15 gold)
topics.say: Fair coin for a fair risk. Tell the harbor folk south you walk under my word.

topics.label: call in the favor for the road
topics.say: Rook off our backs is worth more to me than coin. The road's yours — walk it under my word, and mind the tide.

topics.label: about the archer at the scout line
topics.say: Cal. Good hands, bad debts, and a sister he won't write to. I won't hold him here against his own sense, if he's got any left to find.

topics.label: ask what she makes of the glade now
topics.say: She's quiet a moment before she answers.
fx: "Rested proper. Didn't think I'd live to see it done without fire. Good."
"They swore the oath and meant it. That's Company enough for me — better than a rite I don't understand."
"Burned. The Ironbound way. I gave the order weight I maybe shouldn't have — some of the Company haven't forgiven it, and I'm not sure I have either."

topics.label: leave her to the map
topics.say: Mind the toll on your way out. Company rules, not mine.

topics.label: the wagon's trade
topics.say: Oil, iron, rope, the odd blade — and every debt anyone in this camp has ever run up. Ask, and if it's in the ledger I'll deal fair.

topics.label: about Cal's debt
topics.say: Dice, mostly. He's good with a bow and terrible with a wager. Ten gold clears him. I'd take it from anyone; I'd rather take it from someone who cares whether he goes home.

topics.label: camp gossip
topics.say: Everyone here's heard the tree groan at night. Half think it's the wind. There's talk of Keepers hiding somewhere deep in the wood, and a fool in the stockade who dug up something he shouldn't have.

topics.label: what she's heard from the Vale
topics.say: Word's come west that the Vale's own grief is settled, quiet-like, no fire in it. Makes a body wonder if that's the easier road here too.

topics.label: what she's heard from the Vale
topics.say: Word's come west that somebody put a blade through the Vale's own hollow king. Blunt work. Some in camp respect it more than they'll say.

topics.label: what she's heard from the Vale
topics.say: Word's come west that the Vale's grief was left to sit, neither rested nor answered. Half the camp thinks that's cowardice. I'm not so sure.

topics.label: show the gray boar's tusk
topics.say: That's the one's been gutting snares along the north track. Good riddance.

topics.label: small talk with the cook
topics.say: Best thing about this posting is nobody complains about the food. Worst thing is I know why.

th_cal.name: Cal
th_cal.desc: A young man in faded Company colors, more careful with his arrows than with himself.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Cal. I ride with the Company, for what that's worth these days. You've got my sister's look about you — did she send you, or did you just walk the same road she would have?

topics.label: about your sister
topics.say: Lys. Sharper eyes than mine, and our father never once let her prove it. I left so she wouldn't have to watch me not-leaving anymore. Didn't think that through past the leaving part.

topics.label: why the Free Company
topics.say: Coin, mostly, and a camp that doesn't ask what you're running from. I owe the wagon more than I've got, and I keep telling myself the next contract fixes that.

topics.label: tell him to go home to the Vale (will)
topics.say: He looks at the arrows, not at you, while he thinks it over.
fx: "...Yeah," he says, and sets the bow down like it costs him something. "Yeah, all right. Tell her I'm coming, so she doesn't come looking first."
"Not yet," he says, and picks the bow back up. "Debts don't forgive themselves. Ask me again."

topics.label: let him make his own choice and stay
topics.say: "Good," he says, quiet, and means it. "I'd rather fight for the captain than run from my own debts. Tell Lys that, if you see her before I do."

topics.label: leave him to his arrows
topics.say: Watch the road for me, if you're headed east.

th_fenn.name: Fenn
th_fenn.desc: A wiry man, dirt under every nail, watching you with the patient look of someone who has already decided you're worth talking to.

topics.label: why are you caged
topics.say: Desertion, they wrote. I call it digging where the captain didn't want dug. Forty years of Company men have called this ground cursed and none of them asked why.

topics.label: what you found digging
topics.say: Old muster rolls, half-rotted, from the year of the hanging. The mutiny charge was signed by one officer alone, and he came into money right after. That's not proof of murder. It's proof somebody lied.

topics.label: where the proof might be
topics.say: A pardon was drafted at Marrowgate, I'd swear it on my own neck. It never reached the men it named. If it went anywhere, it went into Bray's dead-letter box — nobody empties that thing.

topics.label: leave him to the cage
topics.say: Mind the guard doesn't hear the rest of it from someone else first.

th_rook.name: Rook
th_rook.desc: A lean man in mismatched Company colors, hand already on a knife.
onDeath: Rook goes down still reaching for the knife. His blade's better kept than the rest of his gear — yours now.
Rook was already square with the camp.

topics.label: what do you want
topics.say: What's owed me. I skim the tolls Camp Gallows won't pay a poacher for good work. Pay it forward, fight me for it, or talk me out of it — your road, your choice.

topics.label: pay him off (6 gold)
topics.say: He counts it twice, then steps clear of the trail without another word.

topics.label: talk him into the Company proper (will)
topics.say: He looks you over like he's pricing you, not the offer.
fx: "...Company's better odds than a solo cut," he admits, and hands over his own blade as a kind of oath. "Tell Vane I'm done freelancing."
"Not interested," he says flat, and doesn't move. It can be tried again.

th_sergeant.name: the gray sergeant
th_sergeant.desc: Forty years gray, a noose-shaped collar of old rope still at his neck.
onDeath: The sergeant comes apart into rag and gray dust. Whatever kept him standing this post finally lets go.

th_rowan.name: Keeper Rowan
th_rowan.desc: Bark-brown hands, patient as a tree is patient, which is to say not very, underneath it.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: One of the last who still keeps the old covenant. We don't sell what we know — we teach it, when someone's earned the asking.

topics.label: the old covenant
topics.say: Every barrow, every hollow place, once had a keeper who spoke for the dead so the living wouldn't have to. The Reeve's line let that lapse, hold by hold. We're what's left of remembering how.

topics.label: the Hanged Company
topics.say: Forty years unrested and nobody's spoken a proper verse over them in all that time. The Reeve's justice and the truth are not always the same animal. This time they weren't.

topics.label: ask to be taught the rest-verse
topics.say: Rowan studies you a long moment, then recites it once, slow, until you have it by heart: a verse for the wrongly hanged, older than the tree that hangs them still.

topics.label: tell Rowan the glade burned
topics.say: Rowan is quiet long enough that you start to wonder if they heard you. "Fire keeps nothing. Not even the truth of what it burns." They don't raise their voice, which is somehow worse.

topics.label: leave the Understory
topics.say: Go careful. The old wood doesn't forgive twice, and neither do we.

th_boar.name: gray boar
th_boar.desc: Blight-pale and heavier than any boar has a right to be, tusks already lowered.
onDeath: The boar goes down hard. One tusk breaks free clean — Sergeant Coe might know it.

descs: Old growth presses close on every side, black bark and gray moss, and the trail keeps its own counsel.

spots.name: Spoil Verge
spots.desc: Scrub and spoil-dust drift down off the Iron Downs, gray on the old leaf-mold. A deer track bends east; the wood thickens south.

spots.name: The High Holloway
spots.desc: A sunken holloway, root-walled, deep enough to hide a wagon in. It runs west and east along the ridge; south the ground drops toward thicker wood.

actions.label: dig at a loose root
fx: Something bright glints under the root — two old coins, dropped or hidden, it's all the same to you now.

spots.name: Cairn Rise
spots.desc: Ground humped and uneven underfoot, old grave-shapes gone soft under centuries of leaf-fall. North a paler mound breaks the pattern, its mouth a chink of old stone. The holloway runs west; wood thickens south and east.

spots.name: Ridge's End
spots.desc: The ridge runs out in broken ground and a long view north over gray spoil-heaps that were never Thornwold's own. South the trees close again; west the holloway continues.

spots.name: Black Thorn Stand
spots.desc: Thornbrake grows close and black here, older than the rest of the wood. A gap shows north between the thorns, and past it, nothing you can quite focus on. West, past a stand of alder, a thread of smoke rises. South and east the ordinary wood resumes.

spots.name: Deer Break
spots.desc: A trampled break in the bracken where deer bed down, though none are here now — gray droppings, old and dry. The wood presses close on every side.

spots.name: The Split Beech
spots.desc: A beech split clean by old lightning, half of it still stubbornly green. Paths run every way from here, trampled by something heavier than deer.

spots.name: The Rope Larder
spots.desc: Snares hang from low branches, most sprung and empty, one not. A cookfire smokes low behind a fallen trunk.

spots.name: Camp's Shadow
spots.desc: The palisade's shadow falls long here of an evening. Trampled grass shows where sentries cut the corner on their rounds. North the ridge rises; south the ground softens toward a stream.

spots.name: The Listening Break
spots.desc: The birdsong stops here, all at once, the way it does before weather — except there is no weather coming. West the wood stands unnervingly still. North and south the ordinary trees resume; east a thicket opens back toward easier ground.

spots.name: Root Tangle
spots.desc: Roots break the ground in every direction, thick as a man's waist, off a tree too tall to see the top of from here. Bitter bark peels loose where the wood has scarred over an old wound.

spots.name: The Heartwood Hollow
spots.desc: A shallow bowl in the land where the oldest trees stand thickest, canopy closed enough to dim midday to dusk.

spots.name: Fox Crossing
spots.desc: A well-used game trail crosses here, fox-scent sharp on the air. East the trees start to thin toward camp; every other way the wood holds close.

spots.name: Wood's Edge
spots.desc: The trees begin to thin, cut back by Company axes. East, past the last of the old growth, Camp Gallows' palisade shows through the branches.

spots.name: The Clawed Rock
spots.desc: The ground drops toward a scatter of gray rock, half-swallowed by bramble. A dark crack shows west in the rockface, wide enough to trouble anyone who has to duck for it. North the wood climbs back toward thicker growth; east it opens onto easier walking.
spots.brief: Bramble and a dark crack west.

spots.name: The Ford Approach
spots.desc: The ground softens, then softens more — a stream is close, though the trees hide it. West a dark crack breaks the rock; east the sound of moving water grows.

spots.name: The River Ford
spots.desc: A stream cuts the wood here, shallow enough to ford but cold enough to make you think twice. Flat stones underfoot are worn smooth by feet older than the Company's camp.

spots.name: Bramble Break
spots.desc: Bramble grows thick and thorned, forcing the path to bend around it rather than through. Every direction looks the same from inside it.

spots.name: The Last Stand
spots.desc: The old growth gives out into younger scrub pine, seeded nobody can say by whom. North the true wood climbs back; west it thickens again.

spots.name: Gull's Reach
spots.desc: Salt shows faint on the wind this far south, though the coast is a long way off yet. East the ground firms toward the south track.

spots.name: Pine Needle Flat
spots.desc: Scrub pine needles carpet the ground thick enough to muffle every step. The wood feels thinner here, closer to its southern edge.

spots.name: The Bluff
spots.desc: The ground rises to a low bluff. South, past a stand of dead pine, a tower's broken crown shows above the canopy — old, and not Company-built. West the pine flat continues; north the true wood climbs back.

onEnter: A gray boar breaks from the brush, tusks first, heavier than any boar has a right to be.

vars.NAME: the Long Watch
vars.VIEW: the whole Thornwold canopy, and past it smoke rising from three neighboring holds

stages.text: Keeper Rowan knows the old rest-verse for the Hanged Company. Ask to be taught it.
The way through the Black Thorn Gap is yours. Go down into the Understory.
Camp gossip speaks of Keepers hidden in the wood. Find the gap in the black thorn.
The true pardon is yours. Read it over the Hanged Company at the gallows glade.
The pardon may be lost in the quartermaster's dead-letter box. Search it (wits).
Fenn in the stockade thinks the Company's hanging was never lawful. Ask what proof he found.
Cal is buried east of Camp Gallows. Lys should hear it from you, gently, when you find her.
Cal is gone, and no grave marks where. There's no good way to say this to Lys.
Cal is at the scout line in Camp Gallows. Persuade him home (will), or clear his debt at the wagon.
A poacher named Rook is skimming Camp Gallows' tolls from a camp in the deep wood. Pay him, fight him, or talk him down.
Captain Vane will trade the smugglers' road for coin, or for Rook dealt with. Ask her.
Captain Vane will sell the smugglers' road under Coldpass for 15 gold, or a favor she'd value more.
Earn Captain Vane's trust first — do right by the Free Companies, then ask her about the road.

epilogue.text: The gallows glade grows green again, slow but sure, and Camp Gallows keeps a quiet toast to the Company each year it turns.
The Free Company swears its oath at the gallows glade every year now, in dead men's names, and means it a little more each time.
The gallows glade is char and bare stone. Camp Gallows doesn't talk about what burned there, or why the dicing never got loud again.
Cal came home to the Vale, and last word had him teaching his sister's old bow-craft to anyone who'd stand still for it.
Cal is buried east of Camp Gallows, marked the way hunters mark a trail, so someone could find him again.
Nobody at Camp Gallows will say what happened to Cal. Lys stopped asking out loud, and started watching the eastern road instead.
The Understory keeps its rite still, one more Keeper's worth of knowing for a stranger who found the gap in the thorn.
Rook and his snares answer to Camp Gallows now, officially this time, and the tolls make it back to the ledger.
